deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is an editorial or archival note about the arrangement of Riemann's philosophical fragments. It is not a working sheet by Riemann.

Handwriting and authorship. The ink hand writes 'Zu den Riemannschen Papieren' ('On Riemann's papers'), which marks it as a later editor's or custodian's note. The likeliest writers are Heinrich Weber or Richard Dedekind, who prepared Riemann's Werke (1876). This attribution is my inference.

Heading. 'Nach Stumpf. (Anordnung und Auswahl der Fragmente)' means 'After Stumpf (arrangement and selection of the fragments)'. Stumpf is presumably the philosopher and psychologist Carl Stumpf, who was in Göttingen around 1870-73. That identification is my inference.

What the note records. It gives a proposed reading order of 14 excerpts, each identified by manuscript page ranges:
1. The marked remark on p. 23.
2. pp. 24-28, with a note on p. 18.
3. pp. 40-44.
4. p. 1 (Causalität, 'causality').
5. p. 38 bottom to p. 40 middle.
6. p. 7 bottom to p. 10 top.
7. p. 2 bottom to p. 3 top.
8. p. 10 bottom to p. 11 middle.
9. p. 1, beginning.
10. p. 40, top to middle.
11. p. 3 middle to p. 6 bottom.
12. pp. 16-17 top.
13. p. 11 middle to p. 16 top.
14. p. 16 middle to p. 21 bottom.

Marginal annotations. Small left-margin numerals '5' (beside item 4) and '4' (beside item 6) propose swapping those two items. Right-margin rubrics appear to assign excerpts to thematic groups: something like 'Psychologie', 'Erkenntnistheoretisches' and 'Grundbegriffe … Physik'. These match the three-part grouping of the published 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' in Riemann's Werke: Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik; Erkenntnisstheoretisches; Naturphilosophie.

Pencil note at the bottom. It appears to be a later archival note listing sheets (Blatt 1-11, Blatt 14 …, Blatt 16, 17). Its first line probably names the fragment 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie' or the natural-philosophy fragments in general.

No computation, derivation or problem appears on the page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics and is not in Riemann's hand. It is an editor's arrangement list for the philosophical fragments, of interest only for the editorial history of the Werke. The 'Stumpf' attribution is a minor detail about who advised on the arrangement.
transcription_corrections: The page is not by Riemann. 'Zu den Riemannschen Papieren' shows it is an editor's or custodian's note.
The left-margin numerals '5' and '4' beside items 4 and 6 indicate a proposed swap of those two items. They are not separate list entries.

The right-margin rubrics are uncertain. They probably correspond to the Werke section titles: 'Psychologie (und Metaphysik)', 'Erkenntnistheoretisch(es)', and something like 'Grundbegriffe der Mechanik/Physik'. The readings 'Erkenntnisbegriff und Psychologie' and 'Grundbegriffe der Mathematik u. Physik' are doubtful.

The first pencil line at the bottom is probably 'Neue math. Princip(ien)' or similar, referring to the fragment 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie', rather than 'Naturphilosophische Fragmente'. The second pencil line ('Blatt 14 von 8.31 …') is largely illegible.
Item 1 reads 'Die angestrichene Bemerkung auf p. 23' ('the marked remark on p. 23'). This is correct.
